chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Safwan and Fadalah from al-Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'When does a man who intends to travel shorten his prayer?' He said, 'When he disappears from the houses.' I said, 'The man intends to travel and leaves when the sun declines (for Dhuhr prayer).' He said, 'When you leave, pray two rak'ahs.'

key_terms.تَوَارَى مِنَ اَلْبُيُوتِ: Disappears from the houses (leaves the city/town)

ai.seo_question: When does a traveler begin shortening their prayers according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* defines the precise moment the legal status of travel begins, establishing that shortening prayers (qasr) commences once the traveler has departed the built-up area of their city. The Imam’s instruction to pray two rak'ahs upon exiting at the time of Dhuhr highlights the practical application of this rule, ensuring the traveler adheres to the shortened form immediately upon entering the state of travel. This ruling is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for determining the validity of qasr based on physical location rather than mere intention.
